## Overview

> **Experimental.** The local IV-GMM interface may change. For the supported
> regression, CATE and conditional-LATE workflows, start with
> [Getting started](getting-started.html) and [Conditional LATE](conditional-late.html).

This vignette shows the local IV-GMM workflow built on `gmm_dnn()`. The example
uses the doubly robust IV moment model created by `gmm_model_dr_iv()` and the IV
simulation DGPs exposed through `sim_iv_data()`.

The localization step uses the shared duplicate-covariate rule: exactly
identical raw X rows receive averaged weights, including redistribution over
surviving block members in each jackknife deletion. Instruments, regressors and
nuisance predictions do not define these groups. The warning about this
modification being outside the paper's theory also applies to GMM; see
[DNN weights and ranks](dnn-weights.html#identical-covariate-rows).

These synthetic IV examples are experimental benchmarks. The paper
replication is described in [Paper replication](paper-affine-replication.html).

## One Local IV Dataset

`sim_iv_data()` returns a data frame with observed variables, oracle nuisance
columns, the target point `x0`, and the true local IV target `theta_x0`.

```{r dgp}
iv <- sim_iv_data(
  design = "dgp2_iv_homog_overid",
  n = 160L,
  kx = 2L,
  q = 2L,
  seed = 1L
)

head(iv$data[, c("X1", "X2", "Z1", "Z2", "D", "Y")])
iv$theta_x0
```

## Fitting the DR-IV GMM Model

The DR-IV model factory records which columns contain the outcome, treatment,
instruments, and nuisance estimates. In this example the nuisance columns are
oracle values generated by the DGP.

```{r fit}
model_iv <- gmm_model_dr_iv(
  y_col = "Y",
  d_col = "D",
  z_cols = c("Z1", "Z2"),
  pi_cols = c("piZ1_oracle", "piZ2_oracle"),
  muY_col = "muY_oracle",
  muD_col = "muD_oracle"
)

fit_iv <- gmm_dnn(
  data = iv$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  x0 = iv$x0,
  model = model_iv,
  k = 1L,
  s = 12L,
  se = TRUE,
  return = "ess"
)

fit_iv$theta
fit_iv$se
fit_iv$J
fit_iv$pval_J
fit_iv$neff
```

`summary()` and `confint()` expose the same fitted object in reporting form:

```{r methods}
summary(fit_iv)
confint(fit_iv)
```

## Optimizer starts and fitted geometry

Each target gets an independent starting value. An explicit `start` vector is
reused for every target; an explicit matrix supplies one column per target.
Either takes precedence over the model's `start(sample, ctx, w, x0)` callback.
Without an explicit start or callback, the optimizer starts at zero; it does
not use the previous target's solution. This avoids an implicit dependence on
target order, but does not guarantee a unique or global optimum.

The fit retains its resolved distance specification and training context for
later weight reconstruction. Replacing a registered distance does not change
that geometry. Custom callbacks that close over mutable external state remain
responsible for reproducible behavior.

## Small IV Simulation

`sim_iv_run()` expands a grid over designs, sample sizes, covariate dimensions,
instrument counts, and Monte Carlo replications. The just-identified design
`dgp1_iv_justid_linear` is always run only once with realized `q = 1`.
An explicit `master_seed` restores the caller's saved RNG state; `NULL` uses
the current stream. Each replicate keeps data and learner draws together.

```{r small-run}
raw_iv <- sim_iv_run(
  designs = c("dgp1_iv_justid_linear", "dgp2_iv_homog_overid"),
  n_vals = 120L,
  kx_vals = 2L,
  q_vals = 2L,
  n_reps = 2L,
  master_seed = 42L,
  k = 1L,
  s_fn = function(n, kx) 10L,
  methods = "iv_oracle",
  verbose = FALSE
)

raw_iv[, c("method", "design", "theta_hat", "se")]
```

These two-replicate cells demonstrate the output format; they are not
coverage evidence. `summarise_iv_results()` aggregates to one row per `(method, design, n, kx, q)`
cell and includes local overidentification diagnostics when `q > 1`.

```{r summary}
tab_iv <- summarise_iv_results(raw_iv)
print(tab_iv, digits = 3)
```
